Rolling-window benchmark, redone with cuplyr

Redo of https://roald-arboel.com/blog/posts/2024/10/03/Benchmark-rolling/ with cuplyr added as one more entry in every statistic panel. Produced by this document (bench/rolling-window.qmd; helpers in bench/rolling-lib.R, installs in bench/install-deps.R): the code that produces every number, table and figure is in the same file as the prose, and every number in the prose is computed from the results. Raw data, written to /home/theo/cuplr/scratchpad/benchmarks/rolling-1e7 on every render: timings.csv, correctness.csv, extension.csv, versions.csv, memory-breakdown.csv, memory-finding.csv, skipped.csv.

Run configuration: cell budget 20 s, probe limit 60 s, times 20, times_custom 5, ext_times 10. Parameters differing from the defaults: n_rows = 10000000 (default 1000000). See “How to render” at the end for the command.

Wall time of the timing chunks, which hold the GPU: 42 min 22 s (bench-main 40 min 41 s, bench-overhead 28 s, bench-ext 34 s, bench-memory 1 s, bench-fence 2 s, bench-runstats-shift 28 s, bench-cores 8 s; the elapsed times of the run that produced the cached results). Every number below is computed in this document from those results.

Read this first: what the numbers are

What cuplyr’s number is. The cuplyr timing is the computation on a table that is already on the GPU: res <- compute(mutate(gt, r = roll_mean(x, n))) followed by gpu_sync() as a fence, with gt <- tbl_gpu(df) built once outside timing. By decision (Theo, 2026-10-21) it contains no upload and no collect(). The CPU packages operate on an R vector already in memory, so both sides time the computation only. A real pipeline that starts and ends in R would also pay the PCIe transfers that are excluded here (not measured in this study). Every cuplyr entry that is timed is computation only. Cells that run on the CPU fallback (download, an R loop, re-upload) are not timed: cuplyr (median, all three widths). The median table and plot carry a note instead of a number for cuplyr.

What the CPU numbers are: measured thread behaviour, not settings. Package thread settings do not say what a call did, so each multi-thread-capable entry (data.table, RcppRoll, roll) was timed twice, at its default setting and with its threads set to one (entries labelled (1 thread)), and the “Threads actually used” section reports both. The result:

  • RcppRoll runs on 24 OpenMP threads by default (RcppRoll::roll_threads() = 24) and scales with them: 7-16x slower at one thread for every statistic at w=101.
  • data.table’s frollmean/sum/min/max/sd and its by= evaluation ran effectively on one thread (default vs setDTthreads(1) within 6.4%), although getDTthreads() is 12. Only frollmedian (2.4x), frollsum(algo = "exact") (6.5x) and frollapply (1.9x) scale.
  • roll ran effectively on one thread for every statistic (1-thread vs default within 1.3% at w=101), although RcppParallel reports 24 available threads. (roll.so also imports seven OpenMP runtime symbols (GOMP*, omp_*), which setThreadOptions() does not govern; the default online vector workers used here are sequential loops, and only roll’s offline workers are RcppParallel workers, so the one-thread reading holds.)
  • RollingWindow, slider, zoo and runner were not given a thread control. Their compiled code imports no OpenMP or TBB runtime symbol (nm -D --undefined-only on the installed shared object, run by this document) and runstats is pure R. I treat them as single-threaded; that is a static check, not a timing.

So there is no blanket “GPU against N CPU threads” framing in this report: the comparison is to the per-entry thread behaviour above. Medians are reported with their spread (IQR in the tables, all samples in timings.csv). No headline speedup is claimed.

What the cuplyr number still includes, per call. R dispatch of mutate()/compute(), the AST node builds and schema inference, lowering to C++, three full-table materializations (an eager window mutate() runs a window node, a mutate node and a select node, each of which builds a new table, so the input column x is deep-copied three times per call; see “Per-call cost breakdown”), allocation of the results and their validity masks, and the fence. The same call on a 1e3-row table, where kernel time is negligible, takes about 2.0 ms for window functions (a plain mutate(y = x + 1) takes 1.1 ms). That floor is about 54% of the 3.80 ms measured at 1e7 rows / width 11 and smaller than the whole data.table call (18.6 ms). The copy and allocation part grows with the row count and is inside every 1e7 and 1e7 cuplyr timing but not in the 1e3-row floor.

Method

  • Data: rw_data(n) (set.seed(12345) by default, then rnorm(n)) with n = 1e7, no NAs, widths 11 / 101 / 1001, right-aligned, output the same length as the input, NA padded. Same functions and arguments as the post (see rw_functions() in bench/rolling-lib.R), times = 20, times = 5 for the custom function.
  • Deviation 1, one harness for everyone. The post used microbenchmark(times = 20), which interleaves expressions and does not force a GC. Here every function (CPU packages and cuplyr) goes through rw_time(): untimed warmup calls, then times samples; an untimed gc() runs before every call with the previous result already dropped; each sample is timed with microbenchmark::get_nanotime(). cuplyr is given the gc() too: an eager mutate() holds its GPU intermediates until R finalizes their pointers (finding F1), and twenty back-to-back 1e7-row calls without it did not run the 12 GB card out of memory in this run, but the intermediates still pile up until a collection. Applying the same gc() to everyone keeps the comparison symmetric. Consequence: no GC ever lands inside a timed region, which in the post’s interleaved harness it sometimes did, and deallocation of each result is untimed for every engine (cuplyr’s GPU tables are freed with cudaFree inside that untimed gc(); the CPU packages’ vectors likewise). A test (tests/testthat/test-bench-F54-harness-extra.R) pins that gc() runs before every call and outside the timed region.
  • Deviation 2, GPU completion. cuplyr’s API gives no “work finished” guarantee (cuplyr exports gpu_sync() (a device-wide wait), but the verbs return once their work is queued). The timed closure ends with cuplyr::gpu_sync(), which waits for all queued GPU work (no copy back to the host). The fence adds under 1 ms (chunk bench-fence timed the rolling mean at 1e7 rows, w=101, in 6.59 ms with the fence and 6.09 ms without, 10 interleaved pairs, median paired difference 0.504 ms); the call without the fence returns once the work is queued, so it times the launch only, and the difference is the GPU time the fence waits for.
  • Deviation 3, slow cells get fewer samples (cell_budget = 20 s of timed work per cell). Each cell starts with one cold probe call; its duration sets the sample count through rw_plan_cell() (bench/rolling-lib.R). A cuplyr cell has one more untimed call before that one, the native probe of the fallback check below, so its “cold” call is its second call and it gets one more warm-up call than the CPU packages. The probe call is not a recorded sample (unless it alone exceeds probe_limit = 60 s, which three cells did); warmup calls (2; 1 above 5 s; 0 above 15 s) and then k timed calls follow, and the note column of timings.csv records exactly this per cell. Every cut is listed in the times cuts table.
  • Deviation 4, runstats alignment moved out of timing. runstats::RunningMean/RunningSd return left-aligned windows (the window starts at i; the last n - 1 values are NA). The timed closure returns that raw result and only tags it in place (attr(out, "rw_align") <- "left", plus the window width in rw_window, on the local fresh vector: no copy). rw_normalize() shifts tagged output to right-aligned, outside timing, before the correctness check. So runstats is timed as the package returns it: mean 120 ms, sd 334 ms at w=101 in the results tables. Chunk bench-runstats-shift timed the same two calls again with the shift inside the call, interleaved with the unshifted calls (20 pairs per statistic; these are that chunk’s own samples, not the tables’). In those pairs the shift adds 92.5 ms to the mean call (141 ms unshifted, 207 ms shifted) and 68.3 ms to the sd call (362 and 402 ms), so the shift is a sizeable part of the mean figure. The unshifted figures of that chunk agree with the tables’.
  • Deviation 5, argument choices the brief left open. RcppRoll::roll_medianr(fill = NA) is used (right-aligned; plain roll_median is centred). The custom function is sum_custom <- function(x) sum(x), a naive window sum (my reading of “unoptimised”; I did not have the post’s exact body). Calls: data.table::frollapply(x, n, sum_custom) and zoo::rollapply(x, n, sum_custom, fill = NA, align = "right").
  • Single-thread controls. data.table (1 thread) is setDTthreads(1) for the cell (restored afterwards); RcppRoll (1 thread) is options(RcppRoll.threads = 1); roll (1 thread) is RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = 1) (restored to "auto"). The one-thread entry is timed right after its default-thread entry on the same data, through the same harness, and is also checked for correctness. Thread settings as found, before any change: OMP_NUM_THREADS unset, getDTthreads() 12, RcppRoll::roll_threads() 24, RcppParallel::defaultNumThreads() 24 (versions.csv).
  • Correctness check (not in the post). Results are computed outside timing, normalized (as.numeric, runstats shifted, left-pad with NA) and compared with data.table::froll<stat> via all.equal(tolerance = tol) (tol = 1e-08) plus identical NA positions. cuplyr results are collected for this check only. A cell whose call errors counts as a failure in the table (it does not drop out of the count); there were none.
  • Fallback check. Every cuplyr cell is probed before it is timed: one untimed call under options(cuplyr.fallback = "error") (rw_native_probe() in bench/rolling-lib.R). A cell whose probe call falls back to the CPU (cuplyr’s “fell back to CPU evaluation” error) is not timed, not checked for correctness and not plotted; it is recorded in the skipped-cells table below and in skipped.csv. A probe call that fails for any other reason is not a skip: in the main and extension experiments the cell is recorded as failed (an error row, which counts against the correctness total), and in the overhead, memory and fence chunks it stops the render. Three cells were skipped in this run: cuplyr (median, all three widths); they are listed in the table below and in skipped.csv. As a second check the timed cells catch cuplyr_cpu_fallback conditions: none was raised by a timed cell.
  • cuplyr entries: cuplyr is native roll_<stat>(x, n) inside mutate(); cuplyr (froll alias) is data.table::froll<stat>(x, n) inside mutate() (cuplyr maps it to the same kernel; the alias was 0.000514-0.0604 ms slower than native in each of the 15 cells, i.e. within 0.1 ms). There is no cuplyr median entry: roll_median() has no cudf kernel in 25.12 and runs through an R loop on collected data, so it is not timed. Custom: n/a (cuplyr cannot apply an arbitrary R function over windows).
  • Comparison words. Two medians are “level” when they are within 5% of each other, unless their interquartile ranges do not overlap, in which case one is “slightly faster” than the other; outside that band they are “faster” and “slower”. A cost “grows” with the window width when the median at w=1001 is at least 1.5 times the median at w=11 (it “shrinks” at the inverse ratio and is “flat” in between); slider is “growing” above 1.1 times. An entry “scales” with threads at a one-thread over default ratio of at least 1.5, and does not at 1.15 or less. Two figures “agree” within a factor of 1.25; a slow core is measurably slower above 1.2 times; two calls “cost the same” within 10%; a custom function is clearly slower above 10 times its optimized equivalent; the narrow-window call is “mostly call chain” when it is within 25% of the cumsum mutate; a peak is “well inside” the card below 25% of its memory. cuplyr’s rank among the entries is “near the front” when its rank divided by the number of entries is at most 0.25, “near the back” at 0.75 or more and “mid-pack” in between; the runstats alignment shift is “a sizeable part” of the mean figure when it adds more than 10% to it.

Reading it:

  • RcppRoll scales on every statistic (7.1-16.4x slower at one thread at w=101; 9.7x at 1e7 rows). Its 24-thread numbers are what the “RcppRoll” rows in the tables show.
  • data.table scales only for frollmedian (2.4x), frollsum(algo = "exact") (6.5x) and frollapply (1.9x). frollmean/sum/min/max/sd (ratio 0.98-1.00) and the grouped by = g call (0.94) do not: that is the figure the grouped comparison below depends on.
  • roll does not scale on any statistic (ratio 0.99-1.01), including at 1e7 rows.

Thread settings as found: OMP_NUM_THREADS unset; data.table::getDTthreads() 12; RcppRoll::roll_threads() 24; RcppParallel::defaultNumThreads() 24.

Core placement. This CPU mixes core types (16 logical CPUs at up to 5100 MHz, 8 at up to 3900 MHz), and the benchmark does not pin threads, so a single-threaded call can land on either kind. Chunk bench-cores pinned RcppRoll’s one-thread rolling mean (w=101) to each kind in turn: 76.9 ms on a fast core and 141 ms on a slow one, so landing on a slow core can cost a single-threaded call up to 1.8x, which is what pinning shows for this one. Which kind of core each benchmark timing ran on is not recorded. The calls that run on one thread, default-thread rows included, are exposed to this: roll, RollingWindow, slider, zoo, runner and runstats; data.table’s frollmean/sum/min/max/sd; the (1 thread) controls; and cuplyr’s host-side R work. The calls the threads table shows using more than one thread (RcppRoll; data.table’s frollmedian, frollsum(algo = "exact") and frollapply) can use both kinds of core.

Cross-check of the one-thread RcppRoll mean at w=101: 83.7 ms in the results table, 77.7 ms scaled to 1e7 rows from the 1e7-row run, 76.9 ms on a fast core and 141 ms on a slow one. The table figure agrees with the 1e7-row rate and the fast-core figure within a factor of 1.25 and is 1.68x away from the slow-core figure, so this render’s one-thread RcppRoll cell ran at fast-core speed. data.table’s default and one-thread timings of its single-threaded calls (frollmean/sum/min/max/sd) are within 2.0% of each other. The runstats mean call, timed in two chunks of this render, took 120 ms in the results table and 141 ms in chunk bench-runstats-shift.

Install results

Everything the benchmark needs is installed; nothing is “not run: install failed”. It took five install runs because the pixi environment puts a conda gcc first on PATH, and that gcc cannot link against the distro R’s Makeconf (-latomic_asneeded unknown, __libc_csu_init missing from the conda sysroot): every package that links Fortran/BLAS (quadprog, RcppArmadillo) or configures TBB (RcppParallel, hence roll) failed in the first runs. bench/install-deps.R now:

  1. puts /usr/bin first on PATH and sets CC/CXX/FC to the system compilers for the install only (override: BENCH_PIXI_TOOLCHAIN=1);
  2. points RcppParallel at the distro’s TBB (TBB_INC/TBB_LIB);
  3. installs fftwtools (a runstats dependency; tarball installs do not resolve dependencies) and RcppArmadillo before the runstats tarball;
  4. builds RollingWindow with a temporary user Makevars that drops -Werror=format-security (its generated RcppExports.cpp trips it on current Rcpp).

Logs, in order, with the packages whose install failed in each (read from the summary table at the end of each log in /home/theo/cuplr/scratchpad/benchmarks/rolling-1e7):

log failed note

A single clean run from an empty library was not repeated, so reproducibility from scratch rests on those incremental runs. The installer script’s last edits (the finally = that unsets the temporary Makevars variable, and knitr and rmarkdown added to cran_pkgs) have not been exercised by an install run: nothing was reinstalled. Base install.packages() only; nothing went into the pixi library and cuplyr was not installed. knitr 1.51 and rmarkdown 2.31, which this document needs, are listed in bench/install-deps.R; they were found in /home/theo/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6 (not the benchmark library), and rendering this document installs nothing.

Correctness

Every timed (statistic x function x width) cell, including every timed cuplyr entry and every one-thread control, was compared with data.table’s result. Reference: frollmean/frollmedian/frollmin/frollmax/frollsum/frollsd, and frollsum for the custom sum.

213 of 213 (function x width) cells match data.table (all.equal tol 1e-08, same NA positions). The denominator counts the cells that were timed. Three planned cells were skipped as CPU fallbacks and are neither timed nor checked, so the count is 213, not 216.

No cuplyr mismatch, and none for any other package. “Match” includes the leading NA padding after normalization (runstats after the right-alignment shift in rw_normalize()); a padding or sd-convention difference would have shown up as a mismatch. Not covered: data with NAs, na.rm = TRUE, non-default alignment.

Per-call cost breakdown (overhead)

Measured on the same harness as everything else (gc-separated, fenced, compute() of an eager mutate()), on a 1e3-row table (kernel negligible; 50 samples) and, for contrast, on the 1e7-row table (20 samples). The per-statistic 1e3-row rolling floors are listed too.

call rows median_ms_iqr min_max_ms n

cuplyr (1e3-row overhead floor) [mean] 1,000 2.05 (2.04-2.05) 2.01-2.11 50

  • The about-2.0 ms floor is for window-function mutates; a plain mutate is about 1.1 ms. At 1e3 rows: plain mutate(y = x + 1) 1.10 ms, mutate(r = cumsum(x)) 1.73 ms, mutate(r = roll_mean(x, n)) 2.04 ms (the five rolling statistics: 1.99-2.30 ms medians; all 250 samples between 1.93 and 2.52 ms). cumsum and roll_mean differ here (1.73 vs 2.04 ms), so part of the extra 0.9 ms may belong to the kernel rather than to the window-function path.
  • What the path does (read from the code, confirmed with show_query()). A plain mutate is one node (ast_mutate <- ast_source). An eager window mutate is ast_select <- ast_mutate <- ast_window <- ast_source (R/mutate.R lines 641, 645 and 655 push the window, mutate and select nodes), and an eager call runs that chain as one execution (push_chain() in R/execute.R, F57): the nodes’ outputs share the input table’s columns instead of deep-copying them (src/ops_window.cpp about line 1205 passes the input columns through as shared pointers), so only the computed columns are allocated. Before F57 each node built a full table and x was copied three times per call. The per-node R work (node build, schema inference) is still done three times; I did not profile where the 0.9 ms goes at 1e3 rows. GPU memory shows it, though not to the byte (1e7 rows, memory-breakdown.csv; the decomposition below differs from the measured total by 483,750,144 B):
call n_rows x_column_bytes allocated_bytes held_after_call_bytes peak_bytes held_after_gc_bytes
window mutate(r = roll_mean(x, 101)) 10,000,000 80,000,000 893,122,100 81,250,048 530,000,054 81,250,048
plain mutate(y = x + 1) 10,000,000 80,000,000 80,000,220 80,000,000 80,000,220 80,000,000
window mutate(r = cumsum(x)) 10,000,000 80,000,000 280,103,264 80,000,000 280,000,004 80,000,000

The 81,250,048 B held right after a roll_mean mutate are compared here with the three tables the node chain built before F57 (one per node, 161,250,048 (window output: x + ..win1.. + validity mask) + 242,500,096 (mutate output: x + ..win1.. + r + two masks) + 161,250,048 (select output, the result) = 565,000,192); F57 executes the chain once and shares the input columns, so the measured figure is expected to be far below that sum. The decomposition is reasoned from the node chain and sized from the column bytes (8 bytes per row per column) and the padded validity mask; it differs from the measured total by 483,750,144 B. I did not measure the three tables separately. A plain mutate holds 80,000,000 B (x copy + y, one materialization; the node chain predicts 160,000,000) and allocates 80,000,220 B in total, against 893,122,100 B allocated by one roll_mean mutate. After a gc() the roll_mean result alone is 81,250,048 B, so about 1.0x the result is held while the intermediates await finalization. The copy and allocation cost scales with rows and is inside every 1e7 and 1e7 cuplyr timing. At 1e7 rows the plain mutate takes 1.39 ms (+0.29 ms vs 1e3 rows), the cumsum window mutate 3.10 ms (+1.37 ms) and roll_mean(x, n) 6.59 ms (+4.55 ms). The narrow-window rolling mean (w=11, 3.80 ms in the tables above) is only 0.692 ms above the cumsum mutate: at narrow widths, most of cuplyr’s time at this size is the call chain and the copies, not the rolling kernel. (This is an inference from comparing two different kernels, not a profile.)

Conclusions (in the post’s style, updated)

All figures: 1e7 rows, width 101, median ms, computation only. cuplyr excludes transfers. Thread behaviour of the CPU entries is the measured one in “Threads actually used”: RcppRoll ran on 24 OpenMP threads; data.table’s frollmean/sum/min/max/sd and its by= evaluation ran effectively on one thread; roll ran effectively on one thread; data.table’s frollmedian, frollsum(algo = "exact") and frollapply scale.

  • The post’s headline (“data.table wins”) holds (with an exception, below) at equal, one-thread conditions; RcppRoll’s lead at default settings comes from its 24 OpenMP threads. At default settings RcppRoll was the fastest package in every statistic: mean 11.6 ms (data.table 18.6), sum 11.8 ms (data.table 18.4), min 11.8 ms (data.table 28.1), max 11.7 ms (data.table 27.8), sd 12.1 ms (data.table 115), median 40.4 ms (data.table 194). With RcppRoll.threads = 1 it takes mean 83.7, sum 83.3, min 118, max 118, sd 107 and median 664 ms (7-16x slower). Against that one-thread RcppRoll, data.table (whose mean/sum/min/max calls are single-threaded anyway) compares as follows, with both at one thread: mean, max and median: faster at all three widths; sum and min: slightly faster at w=11, faster at w=101 and w=1001; sd: slower at all three widths. For the median, data.table at one thread takes 298 / 472 / 673 ms (RcppRoll at one thread: 365 / 664 / 957); RollingWindow’s median (349 / 543 / 684 ms) compared with data.table at one thread is behind at w=11 and w=101, slightly behind at w=1001. Even with its 12 threads data.table’s median (194 ms) is about 4.8x slower than the 24-thread RcppRoll (40.4 ms). sd is the exception: RollingWindow (92.0 ms) is fastest, then one-thread RcppRoll (107) and one-thread data.table (113); the post had no data.table sd.
  • roll (48.8 ms mean, 40.2 sum, 113 min/max, 239 sd, 2030 median) is a reasonable choice for the statistics it covers, but data.table 1.18 now has frollmedian and frollsd and beats it on those (at one thread, too: median 472 vs 2030 ms, sd 113 vs 242). roll ran on one thread for every statistic.
  • slider (489-548 ms at w=101; 278-305 ms at w=11, 691-781 ms at w=1001, growing with the width) is for custom alignment, not speed. zoo (2.1-5.6 s) and runner (6.9-10 s at w=101, 32-67 s at w=1001) are slow. Custom functions cost 12.9 s (frollapply; 24.0 s at one thread) and 43-152 s (zoo::rollapply, growing with the width) against 18 ms for the optimized equivalent (data.table’s frollsum). Avoid them.
  • Where cuplyr lands (ungrouped, 1e7 rows). Native mean/sum/min/max take 3.2-3.8 / 6.2-6.6 / 6.2-6.5 ms at widths 11 / 101 / 1001, of which about 2.0 ms is the per-call floor for window mutates. For mean, per competitor (median at w=101 in parentheses): against data.table (18.6), data.table (1 thread) (18.2), 24-thread RcppRoll (11.6), RcppRoll (1 thread) (83.7), roll (48.8), roll (1 thread) (49.2), RollingWindow (74.0), runner (9780), runstats (120), slider (491) and zoo (2070), cuplyr is faster at all three widths. For sum against roll, cuplyr is faster at all three widths (6.37 vs 40.2 ms at w=101). For min and max it beats data.table at every width (cuplyr vs data.table at w=11: 3.21 vs 39.0 ms for min and 3.20 vs 38.8 ms for max). cuplyr sd takes 11.7 / 11.4 / 11.4 ms: fastest at w=11, fastest at w=101 and fastest at w=1001. cuplyr roll_median() is not timed: it has no GPU path and runs on the CPU fallback, so it is left out of every figure here (F3). Custom functions: not supported.
  • cuplyr’s cost does not grow strongly with the window width (mean 3.80 / 6.58 / 6.54 ms; sd 11.7 / 11.4 / 11.4 ms) while data.table’s mean/sum/sd/median, roll’s mean/sum/min/max/sd and 24-thread RcppRoll’s mean/sum/min/max/sd are flat in the width (data.table’s min/max get faster with the width; data.table’s exact sum, roll’s median and 24-thread RcppRoll’s median get slower). That is not the pattern a kernel that rescans each window would produce. I did not read or profile the kernel (F2).
  • Grouped data and large data, in the configurations measured here. Grouped mean (one configuration: 1e6 rows, 1e3 groups, w=101): cuplyr 2.58 ms vs data.table by group 30.7 ms and slider 56.0 ms, so cuplyr is about 12x faster than data.table and about 22x faster than slider, computation only. data.table’s by= evaluation ran effectively single-threaded (30.7 ms by default, 28.7 ms at setDTthreads(1)), so the 12x is the GPU against one CPU thread making 1,000 per-group calls, not against 12 threads. I did not vary the group count; data.table’s cost is expected to grow with the number of groups, so the ratio is specific to 1e3 groups. At 1e7 ungrouped rows (one size) cuplyr is fastest at w=11 (3.83 ms vs data.table 13.0, roll 40.0 and 24-thread RcppRoll 7.38; one-thread RcppRoll 14.7), w=101 (6.60 ms vs data.table 12.6, roll 39.6 and 24-thread RcppRoll 8.02; one-thread RcppRoll 77.7) and w=1001 (6.58 ms vs data.table 12.8, roll 39.3 and 24-thread RcppRoll 8.07; one-thread RcppRoll 72.2). Peak GPU memory for the 1e7-row call was 530 MB, well inside 12 GB, but see F1.
  • Net: at the post’s size cuplyr is near the front (rank 1 of 12 entries for mean at w=101) and bounded below by about 2.0 ms of per-call cost. In the larger configurations measured it was the fastest entry for the grouped configuration (1e3 groups) and 1e7 rows with windows of 11, 101 and 1001, including against 24-thread RcppRoll at 1e7 rows; that is one grouped configuration, one large size and the widths where it was fastest. All of it only when the data already lives on the GPU.

Findings (candidate backlog rows; nothing was fixed in this feature)

  • F1 (addressed by F57). An eager window mutate materialized three full tables and held them until R’s GC. One eager mutate(r = roll_mean(x, n)) on 1e7 rows runs ast_window -> ast_mutate -> ast_select (R/mutate.R 641, 645, 655); in F54 each node built a new table and src/ops_window.cpp deep-copied every input column, so x was copied three times; F57 runs the chain once and shares the columns (src/ops_window.cpp about line 1205). Right after the call 81,250,048 bytes are held (gpu_alloc_tracking(): held 81,250,048 B, peak 530,000,054 B) = 161,250,048 + 242,500,096 + 161,250,048, against 81,250,048 for the result alone, and 893,122,100 bytes are allocated in total (memory-breakdown.csv, memory-finding.csv). A plain mutate holds 80,000,000 bytes (one materialization). The intermediates are freed only when R finalizes their pointers: twenty back-to-back calls without gc() did not run out of memory at this size on the 12 GB card. The fix (F57) appends the window results to the input table’s shared columns instead of copying every input column, with no full-table copies in the mutate and select steps. The expected effect is to take the 1e7-row call from 81 MB to about 81 MB (1.0x). Freeing per-call intermediates deterministically (or an automatic gpu_gc() and retry on bad_alloc) would remain a separate hardening.
  • F2. Rolling kernels do not slow down strongly with the window width in this run. At 1e7 rows, from w=101 to w=1001, mean goes from 6.58 ms to 6.54 ms and sd from 11.4 ms to 11.4 ms (data.table is flat in the width: 115 ms for sd at w=1001). At 1e7 rows mean at w=1001 takes 6.58 ms for cuplyr vs data.table 12.8 and 24-thread RcppRoll 8.07. The widths do not show strong growth in this run, so there is no evidence of a rescan here. Candidate row (only if the growth shows up in a later run): an incremental mean/sum (prefix sums) and a Welford or sum-of-squares sd, checked against all.equal() at the correctness tolerance (1e-08), or find a cudf aggregation that does not rescan each window (needs a probe).
  • F3. roll_median()’s CPU fallback is an R loop, not measured in this report. roll_apply_generic (R/roll.R) loops in R, and it is not timed anywhere in this report. Candidate rows: (a) cheap, call data.table::frollmedian (192-205 ms here at 12 threads, 298-673 ms at one thread across the three widths) inside the fallback; (b) real, a GPU rolling median (cudf 25.12 has no MEDIAN rolling aggregation).
  • F4. A fixed overhead of about 2.0 ms per eager window-function mutate() on a 1e3-row table (1.1 ms for a plain mutate). About 0.9 ms of the 2.0 is specific to the window path, i.e. the ast_select <- ast_mutate <- ast_window <- ast_source chain (three nodes, three materializations; cumsum costs 1.73 ms against 2.04 ms for roll_mean), which may include part of the kernel’s cost; the rest is the 1.1 ms every eager mutate pays. At 1e7 rows the same chain costs 3.10 ms for cumsum against 1.39 ms for a plain mutate, and the floor is about 54% of the narrow-window rolling cost. Candidate row (same fix as F1): remove the extra materializations, then re-measure the 1e3-row floor; profile the remaining 1.1 ms plain-mutate cost (R dispatch, AST build, schema inference) separately, since I did not.
  • F5 (minor). No documented completion semantics. Since F57 there is a documented gpu_sync() that waits for the device; the verbs themselves still return once their work is queued, so wall-clock timing of cuplyr from R is only meaningful after a wait; the benchmark uses gpu_sync() as its fence (F57 added it; before, a one-row gpu_head() read did the job). Related: x$ptr on a tbl_gpu from outside the namespace returns NULL (tibble’s $), so helper code has to use .subset2().

How to render

Render only through tools/r, because the benchmark holds the GPU and the project has one GPU lock for every R process. From the checkout:

tools/r 'source("bench/rolling-window.R")'

That runs quarto render on this file with params$root set to the checkout, writes rolling-window.html and the CSVs to params$out_dir and keeps the knitr cache of the bench-* chunks in params$cache_dir. Quarto empties the directory given to --output-dir before it renders, and params$out_dir holds the install logs this document reads (and, by default, the cache), so the wrapper renders into a temporary directory and copies the HTML over. Do the same by hand: never pass params$out_dir as --output-dir. A cold run (empty cache) took 42 min 22 s of timed work on this machine; a render with a warm cache re-renders only the prose, tables and figures and takes seconds. Quarto 1.9.38 is used; it is a user install and is not installed or upgraded by anything here.

To try it at smoke size (a few seconds), put the overrides in a YAML file and render this file in place with --execute-params; the keys are the front matter’s params, and with the output and cache directories under /tmp the default cache is left alone:

root: "/path/to/the/checkout"
out_dir: "/tmp/rolling-out"
cache_dir: "/tmp/rolling-cache"
n_rows: 5000
times: 2
times_custom: 1
cell_budget: 1
probe_limit: 5
group_rows: 5000
n_groups: 10
ext_rows: 20000
ext_times: 2
tools/r 'system2(Sys.which("quarto"), c("render", "bench/rolling-window.qmd", "--output-dir", "/tmp/rolling-html", "--execute-params", "smoke.yml"))'

The test tests/testthat/test-parity-F63-qmd-render.R does the same on a copy of this file in a temporary directory, with a clean cache, a prose-only edit, a code edit, an edit of the helper file and a forced rerun in turn (opt in with CUPLYR_BENCH_RENDER=1).

Forcing a full rerun. Set FULL_RERUN <- TRUE before source("bench/rolling-window.R"); it passes -P rebuild:true, which makes the setup chunk set cache.rebuild for the bench-* chunks, so every timing chunk runs again and saves its cache anew (rebuild is not part of the cache key). Do the same by hand with -P rebuild:true (or rebuild: true in the parameters file), or delete the cache directory (/home/theo/cuplr/scratchpad/benchmarks/rolling-1e7/cache). Do not use quarto render --cache-refresh. In a review probe it re-ran none of the timing chunks, switched caching on for every other chunk, the setup chunk included, and left cache and figure directories next to the source; a later render would then restore the setup chunk from that cache instead of running it (reasoned, not run).

What invalidates the cache. A bench-* chunk reruns when any of these change: the chunk’s own code or options; the content (not the modification time) of bench/rolling-lib.R; the content of cuplyr’s R/*.R and src/*.{cpp,cu,cuh,h,hpp} files and of src/Makevars (the compile flags) under params$root; the version of R, of libcudf (25.12.00) or of any package the benchmark uses (cuplyr, data.table, roll, RollingWindow, runstats, slider, RcppRoll, zoo, runner, microbenchmark, ggdist, paletteer, ggtext, ggplot2, scales, patchwork, dplyr, RcppParallel, fftwtools, tibble, knitr and rmarkdown); or any run parameter other than the directories and the rebuild switch (root, out_dir, cache_dir, rebuild). Prose, tables and figures are never cached, so editing them never reruns a benchmark. The cached chunks return plain data frames only: a GPU object left in a cached chunk would be restored as a dead pointer.

Source Code
---

format:

    embed-resources: true

    code-tools: true
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false

  root: ".."
  lib: "/home/theo/cuplr/scratchpad/benchmarks/rlib"
  out_dir: "/home/theo/cuplr/scratchpad/benchmarks/rolling"

  n_rows: 1000000

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Library path first, then cuplyr from the checkout named by params$root: an
# older cuplyr is installed in the user library and must never be the one
# that runs. Nothing is installed.
.libPaths(c(params$lib, .libPaths()))
pkgload::load_all(params$root, quiet = TRUE, debug = FALSE)
source("rolling-lib.R")

n_rows <- as.numeric(params$n_rows)
widths <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))
stopifnot(length(widths) == 3L)
w_lo <- widths[1]; w_mid <- widths[2]; w_hi <- widths[3]
times <- as.numeric(params$times); times_c <- as.numeric(params$times_custom)
cell_budget <- as.numeric(params$cell_budget); probe_limit <- as.numeric(params$probe_limit)
group_rows <- as.numeric(params$group_rows); n_groups <- as.numeric(params$n_groups)
group_width <- as.numeric(params$group_width)
ext_rows <- as.numeric(params$ext_rows); ext_times <- as.numeric(params$ext_times)
stats_run <- as.character(unlist(params$stats))
if (isTRUE(as.logical(params$skip_ext))) {
  stop("skip_ext = true is not supported: the conclusions compare the extension runs")
}
dir.create(params$out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# The knitr cache of the timing chunks is keyed on the chunk code (knitr) and,
# through cache.extra, on the content of rolling-lib.R and of cuplyr's R and
# C++ sources, the versions of everything the benchmark uses, and the run
# parameters (not the directories, which only say where things live).
bench_pkgs <- c("cuplyr", "data.table", "roll", "RollingWindow", "runstats", "slider",
                "RcppRoll", "zoo", "runner", "microbenchmark", "ggdist", "paletteer",
                "ggtext", "ggplot2", "scales", "patchwork", "dplyr", "RcppParallel",
                "fftwtools", "tibble", "knitr", "rmarkdown")
ver <- c(R = paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."), rw_versions(bench_pkgs))
# libcudf is the code the cuplyr timings measure, so it is part of the key too
conda_prefix <- Sys.getenv("CONDA_PREFIX")
cudf_json <- if (nzchar(conda_prefix)) list.files(file.path(conda_prefix, "conda-meta"), pattern = "^libcudf-[0-9]", full.names = FALSE) else character()
cudf_ver <- if (length(cudf_json)) sub("^libcudf-([0-9.]+)-.*$", "\\1", cudf_json[1]) else NA_character_
cudf_ver_short <- sub("^([0-9]+\\.[0-9]+).*$", "\\1", cudf_ver)
key_ver <- c(ver, libcudf = if (is.na(cudf_ver)) "unknown" else cudf_ver)
# `rebuild` only forces a rerun (params$rebuild, which FULL_RERUN in
# bench/rolling-window.R passes); it is deliberately not part of the key
key_config <- params[setdiff(names(params), c("root", "out_dir", "cache_dir", "rebuild"))]
# src/Makevars holds the compile flags of cuplyr's C++ (written by configure)
key_files <- c("rolling-lib.R", rw_cuplyr_sources(params$root), file.path(params$root, "src", "Makevars"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  cache.path = file.path(params$cache_dir, ""),
  cache.extra = rw_cache_key(key_files, key_ver, key_config),
  cache.rebuild = isTRUE(as.logical(params$rebuild))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-main
#| cache: true
#| include: false
# The main experiment: every statistic x width x function, with the
# single-thread controls, the correctness check against data.table and the
# cuplyr entries. Uploads its own table and returns plain data frames only: a
# cached GPU object would come back as a dead pointer.
bench_main <- local({
  t_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  has_pkg <- function(p) requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)
  for (p in c("data.table", "microbenchmark")) if (!has_pkg(p)) stop("required package missing: ", p)
  if (!cuplyr::has_gpu()) stop("no GPU")
  n_rows <- as.numeric(params$n_rows)
  widths <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))
  stats_run <- as.character(unlist(params$stats))

  # thread settings as found, before any control changes them
  thread_info <- data.frame(
    item = c("OMP_NUM_THREADS (env)", "data.table getDTthreads()", "RcppRoll roll_threads()",
             "RcppParallel defaultNumThreads()"),
    version = c(if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("OMP_NUM_THREADS"))) Sys.getenv("OMP_NUM_THREADS") else "unset",
                data.table::getDTthreads(),
                if (has_pkg("RcppRoll")) RcppRoll::roll_threads() else NA,
                if (has_pkg("RcppParallel")) RcppParallel::defaultNumThreads() else NA),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- rw_data(n_rows)
  x <- df$x
  gt <- cuplyr::tbl_gpu(df)
  fns <- rw_functions()
  timing_rows <- list()
  corr_rows <- list()
  skip_rows <- list()
  add_skip <- function(stat, fn, width, reason) {
    skip_rows[[length(skip_rows) + 1]] <<- rw_skip_row("bench-main", stat, fn, width, reason)
  }
  add_cell <- function(stat, fn, width, res) {
    timing_rows[[length(timing_rows) + 1]] <<- data.frame(
      stat = stat, fn = fn, width = width, n_rows = n_rows, sample = seq_along(res$ms),
      ms = res$ms, times = res$times, note = res$note, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    if (!is.null(res$cmp)) {
      corr_rows[[length(corr_rows) + 1]] <<- data.frame(
        stat = stat, fn = fn, width = width, ok = res$cmp$ok,
        n_na_mismatch = res$cmp$n_na_mismatch, max_abs_diff = res$cmp$max_abs_diff,
        fell_back = res$fell_back %||% NA, note = res$note %||% "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
  one_cell <- function(call, extract, times, ref) {
    run_cell(call, extract, times, ref, FALSE,
             cell_budget = params$cell_budget, probe_limit = params$probe_limit)
  }

  for (stat in stats_run) {
    rw_say("== statistic: ", stat)
    stat_fns <- fns[[stat]]
    for (width in widths) {
      rw_say("  width ", width)
      ref <- rw_reference(stat, x, width)
      times <- if (stat == "custom") params$times_custom else params$times

      for (fn_name in names(stat_fns)) {
        f <- stat_fns[[fn_name]]
        rw_say("    ", fn_name)
        cell <- function() one_cell(function() f(x, width), identity, times, ref)
        add_cell(stat, fn_name, width, safe_cell(cell))
        # Single-thread control for every entry whose package can use threads.
        pkg <- rw_threaded_pkg(fn_name)
        if (!is.na(pkg) && has_pkg(pkg)) {
          label1 <- rw_one_thread_label(fn_name)
          rw_say("    ", label1)
          add_cell(stat, label1, width, safe_cell(function() with_one_thread(pkg, cell)))
        }
      }

      if (stat != "custom") {
        variants <- list(list(label = "cuplyr", alias = FALSE))
        if (stat != "median") variants[[2]] <- list(label = "cuplyr (froll alias)", alias = TRUE)
        for (v in variants) {
          cf <- rw_cuplyr_fun(stat, alias = v$alias)
          # No cuplyr cell that runs on the CPU fallback is timed: one untimed
          # probe call under cuplyr.fallback = "error" decides first. A probe
          # that fails for another reason is a failed cell, not a skip.
          pr <- rw_native_probe(function() cf(gt, width))
          if (pr$fallback) {
            rw_say("    ", v$label, ": not timed (CPU fallback)")
            add_skip(stat, v$label, width, pr$reason)
            next
          }
          rw_say("    ", v$label, if (!pr$native) ": probe call failed")
          res <- if (pr$native) safe_cell(function() one_cell(function() cf(gt, width), cuplyr_extract, times, ref)) else
            rw_probe_error_cell(pr)
          add_cell(stat, v$label, width, res)
        }
      }
    }
  }
  rm(gt, df, x)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  list(timings = do.call(rbind, timing_rows), correctness = do.call(rbind, corr_rows),
       skipped = rw_skip_table(skip_rows),
       thread_info = thread_info, secs = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_start)
})
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-overhead
#| cache: true
#| include: false
# Per-call cost: the same cuplyr calls on a small table, where kernel time is
# negligible, so they are the fixed cost of one eager mutate() + compute() +
# fence. A plain arithmetic mutate and a cumsum window mutate are timed next
# to the rolling ones to separate the window chain's extra cost from the bare
# mutate cost. Same harness as everything else (gc-separated, fenced). The
# lazy query plans are captured as text to name the nodes each call builds.
bench_overhead <- local({
  t_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  n_rows <- as.numeric(params$n_rows)
  w <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))[2]
  stats_run <- as.character(unlist(params$stats))
  small_rows <- 1e3
  small_times <- 50
  rows <- list()
  add_rows <- function(stat, fn, width, n, ms, note) {
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <<- data.frame(
      stat = stat, fn = fn, width = width, n_rows = n, sample = seq_along(ms),
      ms = ms, times = length(ms), note = note, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }

  skip_rows <- list()
  add_skip <- function(stat, fn, width, reason) {
    skip_rows[[length(skip_rows) + 1]] <<- rw_skip_row("bench-overhead", stat, fn, width, reason)
  }
  # a probe call that fails for another reason than a CPU fallback stops the
  # render: these timings have no correctness check to record the failure in
  probe_or_stop <- function(pr, what) {
    if (!pr$native && !pr$fallback) stop("bench-overhead: the probe call of ", what, " failed: ", pr$reason, call. = FALSE)
    pr
  }

  gt_small <- cuplyr::tbl_gpu(rw_data(small_rows))
  for (stat in intersect(stats_run, c("mean", "sum", "min", "max", "sd"))) {
    rw_say("== overhead floor: ", stat)
    cf <- rw_cuplyr_fun(stat)
    # every cuplyr cell is probed for a CPU fallback before it is timed
    pr <- probe_or_stop(rw_native_probe(function() cf(gt_small, w)), paste("the", stat, "overhead floor"))
    if (!pr$native) { add_skip(stat, "cuplyr (1e3-row overhead floor)", w, pr$reason); next }
    ms <- rw_time(function() cf(gt_small, w), small_times, warmup = 5)
    add_rows(stat, "cuplyr (1e3-row overhead floor)", w, small_rows, ms,
             "same call on 1e3 rows; kernel time negligible")
  }

  gt <- cuplyr::tbl_gpu(rw_data(n_rows))
  calls <- rw_overhead_calls(w)
  inputs <- list(list(g = gt_small, n = small_rows, times = small_times),
                 list(g = gt, n = n_rows, times = params$times))
  for (inp in inputs) {
    for (nm in names(calls)) {
      rw_say("== overhead: ", nm, " on ", inp$n, " rows")
      of <- rw_overhead_fn(calls[[nm]])
      pr <- probe_or_stop(rw_native_probe(function() of(inp$g)), paste0(nm, " on ", inp$n, " rows"))
      if (!pr$native) { add_skip("overhead", nm, NA, pr$reason); next }
      ms <- rw_time(function() of(inp$g), inp$times, warmup = 5)
      add_rows("overhead", nm, NA, inp$n, ms, "")
    }
  }

  lz <- cuplyr::as_lazy(gt_small)
  plans <- lapply(calls, function(f) utils::capture.output(dplyr::show_query(f(lz))))
  rm(lz, gt_small, gt, inp, of)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  list(timings = do.call(rbind, rows), plans = plans, small_rows = small_rows,
       skipped = rw_skip_table(skip_rows), secs = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_start)
})
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-ext
#| cache: true
#| include: false
# Extension: (a) a grouped rolling mean, (b) a larger ungrouped table. Peak
# and held GPU bytes come from one untimed call per cuplyr entry.
bench_ext <- local({
  t_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  widths <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))
  has_pkg <- function(p) requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)
  ext_list <- list()
  add_ext <- function(experiment, fn, width, n, res, mem = NULL, ok = NA) {
    # a failed cell (safe_cell's error row) has no samples: NA figures
    ms <- res$ms[!is.na(res$ms)]
    q <- function(f) if (length(ms)) unname(f(ms)) else NA_real_
    ext_list[[length(ext_list) + 1]] <<- data.frame(
      experiment = experiment, fn = fn, width = width, n_rows = n,
      median_ms = q(stats::median), q25_ms = q(function(v) stats::quantile(v, .25)),
      q75_ms = q(function(v) stats::quantile(v, .75)), min_ms = q(min), max_ms = q(max),
      times = res$times, peak_gpu_bytes = mem$peak %||% NA_real_,
      held_gpu_bytes_after_call = mem$held %||% NA_real_, correct = ok, note = res$note,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  one_cell <- function(call, extract, ref) {
    run_cell(call, extract, params$ext_times, ref, FALSE,
             cell_budget = params$cell_budget, probe_limit = params$probe_limit)
  }
  skip_rows <- list()
  add_skip <- function(experiment, fn, width, reason) {
    skip_rows[[length(skip_rows) + 1]] <<- rw_skip_row("bench-ext", experiment, fn, width, reason)
  }

  # (a) grouped rolling mean; data.table's own result is the reference
  rw_say("== extension (a): grouped")
  dfg <- rw_grouped_data(params$group_rows, params$n_groups)
  setup <- rw_grouped_setup(dfg, params$group_width)
  g_ref <- setup$data.table$extract(setup$data.table$run())
  grouped_label <- function(nm) switch(nm, slider = "slider (grouped_df)", data.table = "data.table (by = g)", nm)
  for (nm in names(setup)) {
    rw_say("    ", nm)
    e <- setup[[nm]]
    pr <- list(native = TRUE, fallback = FALSE)
    if (nm == "cuplyr") {
      # probed for a CPU fallback before it is timed, like every cuplyr cell;
      # a probe that fails for another reason is a failed cell, not a skip
      pr <- rw_native_probe(e$run)
      if (pr$fallback) { add_skip("grouped mean", "cuplyr", params$group_width, pr$reason); next }
    }
    res <- if (pr$native) safe_cell(function() one_cell(e$run, e$extract, g_ref)) else rw_probe_error_cell(pr)
    mem <- if (nm == "cuplyr" && pr$native) rw_mem_of(e$run) else NULL
    add_ext("grouped mean", grouped_label(nm), params$group_width, params$group_rows, res, mem, res$cmp$ok)
    if (nm == "data.table") {
      rw_say("    data.table (1 thread)")
      res <- safe_cell(function() with_one_thread("data.table", function() one_cell(e$run, e$extract, g_ref)))
      add_ext("grouped mean", "data.table (by = g, 1 thread)", params$group_width, params$group_rows, res, NULL, res$cmp$ok)
    }
  }
  rm(setup, dfg, g_ref, e)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)

  # (b) the larger ungrouped table
  rw_say("== extension (b): ungrouped")
  dfb <- rw_data(params$ext_rows)
  xb <- dfb$x
  gtb <- cuplyr::tbl_gpu(dfb)
  engines <- list(
    cuplyr = NULL,
    data.table = function(x, n) data.table::frollmean(x, n, align = "right"),
    roll = if (has_pkg("roll")) function(x, n) roll::roll_mean(x, n),
    RcppRoll = if (has_pkg("RcppRoll")) function(x, n) RcppRoll::roll_meanr(x, n, fill = NA)
  )
  for (width in widths) {
    refb <- data.table::frollmean(xb, width, align = "right")
    for (nm in names(engines)) {
      rw_say("    ", nm, " width ", width)
      pr <- list(native = TRUE, fallback = FALSE)
      if (nm == "cuplyr") {
        cf <- rw_cuplyr_fun("mean")
        call <- function() cf(gtb, width)
        extract <- cuplyr_extract
        pr <- rw_native_probe(call)
        if (pr$fallback) { add_skip("ungrouped mean", "cuplyr", width, pr$reason); next }
      } else {
        f <- engines[[nm]]
        if (is.null(f)) next
        call <- function() f(xb, width)
        extract <- identity
      }
      cell <- function() one_cell(call, extract, refb)
      res <- if (pr$native) safe_cell(cell) else rw_probe_error_cell(pr)
      mem <- if (nm == "cuplyr" && pr$native) rw_mem_of(call) else NULL
      add_ext("ungrouped mean", nm, width, params$ext_rows, res, mem, res$cmp$ok %||% NA)
      if (nm != "cuplyr") {
        rw_say("    ", rw_one_thread_label(nm), " width ", width)
        res <- safe_cell(function() with_one_thread(rw_threaded_pkg(nm), cell))
        add_ext("ungrouped mean", rw_one_thread_label(nm), width, params$ext_rows, res, NULL, res$cmp$ok %||% NA)
      }
    }
    rm(refb)
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
  }
  rm(gtb, dfb, xb)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  list(ext = do.call(rbind, ext_list), skipped = rw_skip_table(skip_rows),
       secs = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_start)
})
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-memory
#| cache: true
#| include: false
# Memory: bytes allocated and held right after one call (the result is still
# referenced, so held = result + whatever intermediates have not been
# finalized yet), the peak, and the bytes held after a gc() (the result
# alone), for a rolling mean, a plain arithmetic mutate and a cumsum window
# mutate. Then back-to-back rolling calls without gc(): the finding reported
# as F1.
bench_memory <- local({
  t_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  w <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))[2]
  n_ext <- as.numeric(params$ext_rows)
  dfm <- rw_data(n_ext)
  gtm <- cuplyr::tbl_gpu(dfm)
  cf <- rw_cuplyr_fun("mean")
  calls <- rw_overhead_calls(w)
  mem_calls <- stats::setNames(list(
    function() cf(gtm, w),
    function() rw_overhead_fn(calls[[1]])(gtm),
    function() rw_overhead_fn(calls[[3]])(gtm)
  ), c(names(calls)[2], names(calls)[1], names(calls)[3]))
  # every cuplyr call is probed for a CPU fallback before it is measured; a
  # probe that fails for another reason stops the render (there is no
  # correctness check here to record it in)
  skip_rows <- list()
  native <- vapply(names(mem_calls), function(nm) {
    pr <- rw_native_probe(mem_calls[[nm]])
    if (!pr$native && !pr$fallback) stop("bench-memory: the probe call of ", nm, " failed: ", pr$reason, call. = FALSE)
    if (!pr$native) skip_rows[[length(skip_rows) + 1]] <<- rw_skip_row("bench-memory", "memory", nm, NA, pr$reason)
    pr$native
  }, TRUE)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  breakdown <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(mem_calls)[native], function(nm) {
    rw_say("== memory: ", nm)
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
    one <- cuplyr:::gpu_alloc_tracking(mem_calls[[nm]]())
    row <- data.frame(call = nm, n_rows = n_ext, x_column_bytes = 8 * n_ext,
                      allocated_bytes = one$allocated_bytes, held_after_call_bytes = one$held_bytes,
                      peak_bytes = one$peak_bytes, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    rm(one)
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
    after_gc <- cuplyr:::gpu_alloc_tracking({ r <- mem_calls[[nm]](); gc(verbose = FALSE); r })
    row$held_after_gc_bytes <- after_gc$held_bytes
    rm(after_gc)
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
    row
  }))

  # back-to-back calls without gc(); each result is dropped, only unfinalized
  # intermediates linger
  n_calls <- 20
  oom_at <- NA_integer_
  err <- ""
  if (native[[1]]) {
    rw_say("== memory: ", n_calls, " back-to-back calls without gc()")
    for (i in seq_len(n_calls)) {
      r <- tryCatch(cf(gtm, w), error = function(e) { err <<- conditionMessage(e); NULL })
      if (is.null(r)) { oom_at <- i; break }
      rm(r)
    }
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
  }
  first <- function(col) if (native[[1]]) breakdown[[col]][1] else NA_real_
  finding <- data.frame(
    n_rows = n_ext, held_after_one_call_bytes = first("held_after_call_bytes"),
    peak_one_call_bytes = first("peak_bytes"), result_table_bytes = first("held_after_gc_bytes"),
    n_calls = n_calls, failed_at_call = oom_at, error = substr(err, 1, 200))
  rm(gtm, dfm)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  list(breakdown = breakdown, finding = finding, skipped = rw_skip_table(skip_rows),
       secs = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_start)
})
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-fence
#| cache: true
#| include: false
# What the gpu_sync() fence costs: the same rolling-mean call on
# the larger table, with and without it, through the same gc-separated
# harness. The two variants are timed in alternation (rw_time_interleaved), so
# a drift of the machine's state hits both alike.
bench_fence <- local({
  t_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  w <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))[2]
  dfb <- rw_data(as.numeric(params$ext_rows))
  gtb <- cuplyr::tbl_gpu(dfb)
  with_fence <- rw_cuplyr_fun("mean", fence = TRUE)
  without_fence <- rw_cuplyr_fun("mean", fence = FALSE)
  rw_say("== fence on / off")
  pr <- rw_native_probe(function() with_fence(gtb, w))
  # a probe that fails for another reason than a CPU fallback stops the render
  if (!pr$native && !pr$fallback) stop("bench-fence: the probe call failed: ", pr$reason, call. = FALSE)
  if (pr$native) {
    timings <- rw_time_interleaved(list(on = function() with_fence(gtb, w),
                                        off = function() without_fence(gtb, w)),
                                   params$ext_times)
    skipped <- rw_skip_table(list())
  } else {
    timings <- NULL
    skipped <- rw_skip_table(list(rw_skip_row("bench-fence", "fence", "cuplyr", w, pr$reason)))
  }
  rm(gtb, dfb)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  list(timings = timings, skipped = skipped, secs = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_start)
})
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-runstats-shift
#| cache: true
#| include: false
# runstats returns left-aligned windows. The main experiment times the raw
# result (the shift to right-aligned happens outside timing); this chunk times
# the same calls with the shift inside, to show how much the shift would have
# added. The "outside" and "inside" samples are interleaved (one of each per
# round, the order alternating), so the difference is a paired one that a change
# of process state between the two halves of a run cannot fake. These are this
# chunk's own samples, separate from the main table's.
bench_runstats <- local({
  t_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  if (requireNamespace("runstats", quietly = TRUE)) {
    w <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))[2]
    x <- rw_data(as.numeric(params$n_rows))$x
    fns <- rw_functions()
    out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("mean", "sd"), function(stat) {
      f <- fns[[stat]]$runstats
      rw_say("== runstats ", stat, ": shift outside / inside timing, interleaved")
      d <- rw_time_interleaved(list(outside = function() f(x, w),
                                    inside = function() rw_normalize(f(x, w), length(x))),
                               params$times)
      data.frame(stat = stat, shift = d$label, sample = d$sample, ms = d$ms, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  } else {
    out <- NULL
  }
  list(timings = out, secs = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_start)
})
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-cores
#| cache: true
#| include: false
# One-thread timings may depend on which core the scheduler picks when the CPU
# mixes core types (performance and efficiency cores run at different speeds).
# This chunk pins the R process to one fast and one slow logical CPU in turn
# and times one single-thread RcppRoll rolling mean on each. The affinity and
# the RcppRoll thread setting are restored on exit, also after an error. NULL
# when lscpu or taskset is missing. (No cuplyr call here: nothing to probe.)
bench_cores <- local({
  t_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  n_rows <- as.numeric(params$n_rows)
  w <- sort(as.numeric(unlist(params$widths)))[2]
  lscpu <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(system2("lscpu", "-e=CPU,MAXMHZ", stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)), error = function(e) character())
  taskset <- unname(Sys.which("taskset"))
  out <- NULL
  if (length(lscpu) > 1L && nzchar(taskset) && requireNamespace("RcppRoll", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cpus <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(trimws(lscpu[-1]), "\\s+"), function(z) data.frame(cpu = as.integer(z[1]), mhz = as.numeric(z[2]))))
    cpus <- cpus[!is.na(cpus$cpu) & !is.na(cpus$mhz), ]
    cut <- mean(range(cpus$mhz))
    cpus$kind <- ifelse(cpus$mhz >= cut, "fast", "slow")
    pid <- Sys.getpid()
    mask <- sub("^.*: ", "", system2(taskset, c("-p", pid), stdout = TRUE))
    x <- rw_data(n_rows)$x
    restore <- rw_set_threads("RcppRoll", 1)
    rows <- tryCatch(
      lapply(c("fast", "slow"), function(k) {
        pick <- cpus[cpus$kind == k, ]
        if (!nrow(pick)) return(NULL)
        cpu <- pick$cpu[nrow(pick)]
        system2(taskset, c("-cp", cpu, pid), stdout = FALSE)
        rw_say("== core placement: ", k, " cpu ", cpu)
        ms <- rw_time(function() RcppRoll::roll_meanr(x, w, fill = NA), params$times)
        data.frame(kind = k, cpu = cpu, mhz = pick$mhz[nrow(pick)], n_cpus = nrow(pick), ms = ms)
      }),
      finally = {
        restore()
        system2(taskset, c("-p", mask, pid), stdout = FALSE)
      })
    out <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  }
  list(timings = out, secs = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_start)
})
```

```{r}
gpu_gb <- if (!is.null(gpu)) round(gpu$total_memory / 1e9) else NA_real_
gpu_cc <- if (!is.null(gpu)) gpu$compute_capability else NA_character_

# Do the packages that were not given a thread control import an OpenMP or TBB
# runtime? `nm -D --undefined-only` on the installed .so (NA: no nm). OpenMP
# symbols (GOMP, omp_) and TBB symbols are counted apart: roll's TBB calls are
# the ones RcppParallel::setThreadOptions() governs, its OpenMP ones are not.
omp_symbols <- function(pkg) {
  libs <- file.path(find.package(pkg), "libs")
  sos <- list.files(libs, pattern = "\\.so$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(sos)) return(c(compiled = FALSE, symbols = 0, tbb = 0))
  nm <- Sys.which("nm")
  if (!nzchar(nm)) return(c(compiled = TRUE, symbols = NA, tbb = NA))
  syms <- unlist(lapply(sos, function(so) suppressWarnings(system2(nm, c("-D", "--undefined-only", shQuote(so)), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE))))
  c(compiled = TRUE, symbols = sum(grepl("GOMP|omp_", syms)), tbb = sum(grepl("tbb", syms, ignore.case = TRUE)))
}
omp <- t(vapply(c("RollingWindow", "slider", "zoo", "runner", "runstats", "roll", "RcppRoll", "data.table"),
                function(p) if (ver[[p]] == "not installed") c(NA, NA, NA) else omp_symbols(p), c(0, 0, 0)))
colnames(omp) <- c("compiled", "symbols", "tbb")

  package = c("R", "cuplyr", "data.table", "roll", "RollingWindow", "runstats", "slider", "RcppRoll",
              "zoo", "runner", "microbenchmark", "RcppParallel", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "scales",
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| include: false
# Formatting and comparison helpers for the prose. Every figure and every
# comparative word in the text goes through these.

# The thresholds behind the comparison words; "Method" states them from here.
th_level <- 0.05   # medians within this fraction of each other are "level" (unless the IQRs are disjoint)
th_trend <- 1.5    # widest / narrowest window median: at least this is "grows", at most its inverse "shrinks"
th_grow <- 1.1     # slider is "growing with the width" above this ratio
th_same <- 0.1     # two calls "cost the same" within this fraction
th_chain <- 0.25   # the narrow-window call is "mostly call chain" within this fraction of the cumsum mutate
th_x <- 1.25       # two figures that "agree" are within this factor of each other
th_core <- 1.2     # a slow core is "measurably" slower than a fast one above this ratio
th_avoid <- 10     # a custom function is clearly slower above this factor
th_front <- 0.25   # rank / entries at most this is "near the front", at least 1 minus it "near the back", "mid-pack" between
th_part <- 0.1     # the runstats shift is "a sizeable part" of the mean figure above this fraction
th_mem <- 0.25     # peak memory is "well inside" the card below this fraction of it
thr_yes <- 1.5     # one-thread / default ratio at which an entry "scales" with threads
thr_no <- 1.15     # ... and at or below which it does not
# three significant digits, trailing zeros kept (4.00, not 4)
fmt_ms <- function(v) vapply(v, function(z) if (is.na(z)) "NA" else sub("\\.$", "", trimws(formatC(signif(z, 3), format = "fg", digits = 3, flag = "#"))), "")
fmt_2 <- function(v) vapply(v, function(z) if (is.na(z)) "NA" else sub("\\.$", "", formatC(z, digits = 2, format = "fg", flag = "#")), "")
fmt_1 <- function(v) sprintf("%.1f", v)
fmt_x <- function(r, digits = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "fx"), r)
fmt_xr <- function(r) fmt_x(r, if (r >= 10) 0 else 1)
fmt_pct <- function(f, digits = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * f)
fmt_int <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
fmt_mb <- function(b) sprintf("%s MB", formatC(b / 1e6, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ","))
fmt_rows <- function(n) vapply(n, function(z) {
  k <- log10(z)
  if (z >= 1e3 && abs(k - round(k)) < 1e-9) sprintf("1e%d", as.integer(round(k))) else fmt_int(z)
}, "")
ms_s <- function(v) ifelse(v >= 1000, paste(fmt_ms(v / 1000), "s"), paste(fmt_ms(v), "ms"))
# "4.00 ms", or "not timed" for a cell that was skipped or failed
ms_nt <- function(v) ifelse(is.na(v), "not timed", paste(fmt_ms(v), "ms"))
# a signed difference in ms, or nothing when either side is missing
ms_delta <- function(a, b, vs = "") if (anyNA(c(a, b))) "" else sprintf(" (%+.2f ms%s)", a - b, vs)
fmt_dur <- function(secs) vapply(secs, function(z) {
  m <- floor(z / 60)
  if (m < 1) sprintf("%.0f s", z) else sprintf("%d min %02d s", as.integer(m), as.integer(round(z - 60 * m)))
}, "")
num_words <- c("zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
               "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen",
               "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty")
words <- function(n) ifelse(!is.na(n) & n >= 0 & n <= 20 & n == round(n), num_words[n + 1], as.character(n))
ord_words <- c("first", "second", "third", "fourth", "fifth", "sixth", "seventh", "eighth", "ninth", "tenth")
ordinal <- function(n) if (n <= 10) ord_words[n] else paste0(n, "th")
times_word <- function(n) if (n == 1) "once" else if (n == 2) "twice" else paste(words(n), "times")
plural <- function(n, one, many = paste0(one, "s")) if (n == 1) one else many
code <- function(x) paste0("`", x, "`")
join_and <- function(x, conj = "and") {
  x <- as.character(x)
  n <- length(x)
  if (n == 0L) "" else if (n == 1L) x else if (n == 2L) paste(x, collapse = paste0(" ", conj, " ")) else
    paste0(paste(x[-n], collapse = ", "), " ", conj, " ", x[n])
}
cap1 <- function(s) paste0(toupper(substr(s, 1, 1)), substring(s, 2))
range_x <- function(v, digits = 1) {
  r <- range(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  a <- sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), r[1]); b <- sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), r[2])
  if (a == b) paste0(a, "x") else paste0(a, "-", b, "x")
}
range_num <- function(v, digits = 2) {
  r <- range(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  a <- sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), r[1]); b <- sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), r[2])
  if (a == b) a else paste0(a, "-", b)
}
# a range of times as "lo-hi ms" (or s), two significant digits, whole numbers from 100
fmt_rng_one <- function(v) if (v >= 100) formatC(round(v), format = "d") else fmt_2(v)
range_ms <- function(v) {
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  if (!length(v)) return("NA")
  unit <- if (max(v) >= 1000) "s" else "ms"
  if (unit == "s") v <- v / 1000
  a <- if (unit == "s") fmt_2(min(v)) else fmt_rng_one(min(v))
  b <- if (unit == "s") fmt_2(max(v)) else fmt_rng_one(max(v))
  paste(if (a == b) a else paste0(a, "-", b), unit)
}
slash <- function(v) paste(fmt_ms(v), collapse = " / ")
cmp_than <- function(r, hi = 1 + th_level) {      # r = a / b, a and b both times
  if (r >= hi) "slower than" else if (r <= 1 / hi) "faster than" else "level with"
}

# Lookups into the main results
cell_i <- function(stat, fn, width) match(paste(stat, fn, width, sep = "\r"), cells_key)
med <- function(stat, fn, width) cells$med[cell_i(stat, fn, width)]
med_w <- function(stat, fn, ws = widths) vapply(ws, function(w) med(stat, fn, w), 0)
trip <- function(stat, fn, width) {
  i <- cell_i(stat, fn, width)
  c(med = cells$med[i], q25 = cells$q25[i], q75 = cells$q75[i])
}
nsamp <- function(stat, fn, width) cells$n[cell_i(stat, fn, width)]
has_cell <- function(stat, fn, width) !is.na(cell_i(stat, fn, width))
ext_i <- function(experiment, fn, width) which(ext$experiment == experiment & ext$fn == fn & ext$width == width)[1]
ext_med <- function(experiment, fn, width) ext$median_ms[ext_i(experiment, fn, width)]
ext_trip <- function(experiment, fn, width) {
  i <- ext_i(experiment, fn, width)
  c(med = ext$median_ms[i], q25 = ext$q25_ms[i], q75 = ext$q75_ms[i])
}

# a versus b (both c(med, q25, q75), times): lower is faster. Within 5% of each
# other the medians are called level unless the interquartile ranges are
# disjoint, which makes it "slightly" faster or slower.
verdict <- function(a, b, tol = th_level) {
  if (anyNA(c(a[["med"]], b[["med"]]))) return(NA_character_)
  r <- a[["med"]] / b[["med"]]
  if (r < 1 - tol) return("faster")
  if (r > 1 + tol) return("slower")
  if (a[["q75"]] < b[["q25"]]) return("slightly faster")
  if (b[["q75"]] < a[["q25"]]) return("slightly slower")
  "level"
}
is_faster <- function(v) v %in% c("faster", "slightly faster")
is_slower <- function(v) v %in% c("slower", "slightly slower")
vocab_basic <- c(faster = "faster", `slightly faster` = "slightly faster", level = "level",
                 slower = "slower", `slightly slower` = "slightly slower")
vocab_ahead <- c(faster = "ahead", `slightly faster` = "slightly ahead", level = "level",
                 slower = "behind", `slightly slower` = "slightly behind")
# "faster at all three widths" / "faster at w=101 and w=1001, slower at w=11"
runs_txt <- function(v, ws = widths, vocab = vocab_basic) {
  keep <- !is.na(v)
  v <- v[keep]; ws <- ws[keep]
  if (!length(v)) return("not comparable")
  kinds <- unique(v)
  if (length(kinds) == 1L) {
    where <- if (length(ws) == length(widths)) paste("all", words(length(ws)), "widths") else join_and(paste0("w=", ws))
    return(sprintf("%s at %s", vocab[[kinds]], where))
  }
  paste(vapply(kinds, function(k) sprintf("%s at %s", vocab[[k]], join_and(paste0("w=", ws[v == k]))), ""), collapse = ", ")
}
# statistics with the same verdict pattern are described together
pattern_txt <- function(df, vocab = vocab_basic) {
  stats <- unique(df$stat)
  pats <- vapply(stats, function(s) {
    d <- df[df$stat == s, ]
    paste(d$v[match(widths, d$width)], collapse = "|")
  }, "")
  groups <- split(stats, factor(pats, levels = unique(pats)))
  paste(vapply(names(groups), function(p) {
    v <- strsplit(p, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    v[v == "NA"] <- NA
    sprintf("%s: %s", join_and(groups[[p]]), runs_txt(v, widths, vocab))
  }, ""), collapse = "; ")
}
# median per statistic as "mean 0.87, sum 0.87, min 0.97 ..." where equal
# figures share a label ("10.4 min/max")
merge_equal <- function(fn, stats, width = w_mid) {
  vals <- fmt_ms(vapply(stats, function(s) med(s, fn, width), 0))
  runs <- rle(vals)
  ends <- cumsum(runs$lengths); starts <- ends - runs$lengths + 1
  parts <- vapply(seq_along(runs$values), function(i) paste(runs$values[i], paste(stats[starts[i]:ends[i]], collapse = "/")), "")
  parts[1] <- sub("^(\\S+)", "\\1 ms", parts[1])
  paste(parts, collapse = ", ")
}
```

```{r}
  "no GPU path in this run (the probe call fell back to the CPU)"

  ws <- skip_widths(stat, fn)
  at <- if (length(ws) && length(ws) < length(widths)) paste0(" at ", join_and(paste0("w=", ws))) else ""
  paste0("not timed", at, ": ", skip_why(stat))
}
skip_groups <- unique(sk[c("chunk", "stat", "fn")])
skip_summary <- if (!n_skip) "" else join_and(vapply(seq_len(nrow(skip_groups)), function(i) {
  g <- skip_groups[i, ]

  at <- if (all(is.na(d$width))) "" else if (nrow(d) == length(widths) && g$chunk == "bench-main") paste(", all", words(nrow(d)), "widths") else paste0(", ", join_and(paste0("w=", d$width[!is.na(d$width)])))
  sprintf("%s (%s%s)", code(g$fn), g$stat, at)
}, ""))

  paste0("Every cuplyr entry that is timed is computation only. Cells that run on the CPU fallback (download, an R loop, re-upload) are not timed: ", skip_summary, ".",
         if (median_skipped) " The median table and plot carry a note instead of a number for cuplyr." else "")

# ---- run configuration -------------------------------------------------------
cfg_defaults <- tryCatch(rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("rolling-window.qmd")$params, error = function(e) NULL)
cfg_names <- c("n_rows", "widths", "times", "times_custom", "cell_budget", "probe_limit", "group_rows",
               "n_groups", "group_width", "ext_rows", "ext_times", "stats")

  # numbers compare as numbers (the default 1e7 is read from YAML as text)

}, ""))

# ---- threads: what each setting actually did ------------------------------------

               stringsAsFactors = FALSE) })
default_threads <- function(fn) {
  pkg <- rw_threaded_pkg(fn)
  if (is.na(pkg)) return(NA_character_)
  switch(pkg, data.table = paste0(n_dt_threads, " (setDTthreads)"), RcppRoll = paste0(n_rr_threads, " (OpenMP)"),

}

  if (nrow(a) != 1L) return(NULL)

             default_med = a$med, default_q25 = a$q25, default_q75 = a$q75, one_med = b$med, one_q25 = b$q25,

}))

froll_one <- function(entry, statistic) {
  if (entry == "data.table") code(paste0("froll", statistic))
  else if (entry == "data.table (exact)") code("frollsum(algo = \"exact\")")
  else if (entry == "data.table::frollapply") code("frollapply") else code(entry)
}
froll_group <- function(rows) {
  plain <- rows$statistic[rows$entry == "data.table"]
  others <- vapply(which(rows$entry != "data.table"), function(i) froll_one(rows$entry[i], rows$statistic[i]), "")
  join_and(c(if (length(plain)) code(paste0("froll", paste(plain, collapse = "/"))), others))
}

# ---- who is fastest ---------------------------------------------------------------
cpu_bases <- function(stat) {
  f <- unique(cells$fn[cells$stat == stat])
  f[!grepl("1 thread|^cuplyr|exact|::", f)]
}
view_def <- function(stat, width) { b <- cpu_bases(stat); stats::setNames(vapply(b, function(e) med(stat, e, width), 0), b) }
view_1t <- function(stat, width) {
  b <- cpu_bases(stat)
  stats::setNames(vapply(b, function(e) med(stat, if (!is.na(rw_threaded_pkg(e))) rw_one_thread_label(e) else e, width), 0), b)
}

  if (all(rr_default_wins)) "is not explained by its threads (its one-thread control is about as fast)" else
  sprintf("is limited to %s of %s statistics", words(sum(rr_default_wins)), words(n_st))

  else sprintf("%s %s ms, but %s was faster (%s)", s, fmt_ms(med(s, "RcppRoll", w_mid)), win_def[[s]], fmt_ms(min(view_def(s, w_mid))))
}, ""), collapse = ", ")

dt1_rr1_txt <- pattern_txt(dt1_rr1)

dt_single_txt <- if (length(dt_single_stats)) sprintf(" (whose %s calls are single-threaded anyway)", paste(dt_single_stats, collapse = "/")) else ""
```
